review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on (crossFacet, mem_crossFacet, crossFacet_card in Coefficients.lean). I also checked the other user of flipAt (BoolCubeConstant.lean) and the unrelated flipAt in Ising/Colorings.lean. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the proposed simp lemmas would fire as intended or whether they interact with other simp sets in files that import this one. I found no rewrite cycles or competing simp rules, because the file has no simp attributes at all. The findings are about missing simp interface pieces.

findings.declaration: flipAt (and its call sites flipAt_ne, crossRidge_parents)
findings.problem: flipAt has no evaluation lemmas, so every proof that needs its value does `simp [flipAt]`. That unfolds it to Function.update and relies on Function.update simp lemmas (`update_self`, `update_of_ne`) plus side conditions. The call sites are flipAt_ne (line 16), crossRidge_parents (lines 81, 82, 85) and bool_cube_constant (`simp only [d, flipAt, hflip]`). Unfolding exposes the Function.update implementation in each caller. Because `flipAt` is an ordinary def, `simp` will not see through it in downstream goals unless the caller unfolds it. A plain `simp` call therefore cannot normalise `flipAt b i i` or `flipAt b i j` for j ≠ i.
findings.proposed_change: Add two @[simp] evaluation lemmas right after the definition: `flipAt_apply_self : flipAt b i i = !b i` (proved by `Function.update_self`) and `flipAt_apply_of_ne (h : j ≠ i) : flipAt b i j = b j` (proved by `Function.update_of_ne h`). Alternatively, state `flipAt_apply j : flipAt b i j = if j = i then !b i else b j`, as the Ising development already does for its own flipAt. Then replace `simp [flipAt]` and `simp [flipAt, hj]` with `simp` or `simp [hj]`, and make flipAt_ne `simpa using congrFun he i`.
findings.benefit: Callers get one canonical normal form for flipAt values and no longer unfold to Function.update. The proofs in this file and in bool_cube_constant get shorter and don't depend on how flipAt is implemented.

evidence.excerpt: · simpa [flipAt, hj] using h j hj
have hdflip : d = flipAt b i := by simp only [d, flipAt, hflip]
flipAt x σ y = if y = x then !(σ y) else σ y

findings.declaration: crossRidge_card / mem_crossRidge / crossRidge_subset_iff (cross-facet and ridge API)
findings.problem: The membership and cardinality lemmas for crossFacet and crossRidge (`mem_crossFacet`, `crossFacet_card`, `mem_crossRidge`, `crossRidge_card`) are not simp lemmas, and none of the definitions is irreducible or has a simp set. Each proof therefore rewrites by hand: `(mem_crossFacet n b _).mpr ⟨i,rfl⟩`, `rw [crossRidge, Finset.card_erase_of_mem …, crossFacet_card]`, and `change 0 < (crossRidge n b i).card` followed by `rw [crossRidge_card]`. Because crossRidge is a plain def, `simp` can neither compute the card of a ridge nor decide membership, and goals have to be unfolded with `change` and `rw`. The statement `n-1` (natural subtraction) also forces an `omega` after rewriting.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `crossFacet_card` and `crossRidge_card` as @[simp]. Both have a clean left-hand side and a right-hand side that is a simpler term. Mark `mem_crossFacet` and `mem_crossRidge` as @[simp] as well, if the existential form is acceptable as a normal form. Then crossRidge_mem could be `simp`-driven, and the `(mem_crossFacet n b _).mpr ⟨i,rfl⟩` terms could become `by simp`. If `mem_crossFacet` is not made simp, add a specialised `@[simp] lemma mk_mem_crossFacet : (i.val, b i) ∈ crossFacet n b` that covers the repeated `⟨i,rfl⟩` witnesses (lines 21, 31, 64 and LabelRegion.lean line 96).
findings.benefit: Cardinality and membership goals about crossFacet and crossRidge could be closed or normalised by `simp`. The repeated `(mem_crossFacet n b _).mpr ⟨i,rfl⟩` boilerplate would go away, and downstream files would not need to rediscover these lemma names.

evidence.excerpt: lemma crossFacet_card (n : ℕ) (b : Fin n → Bool) : (crossFacet n b).card = n
v ∈ crossFacet n b ↔ ∃ i : Fin n, v = (i.val,b i)
